From: Julian Morris <jmorris@avahealth.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 14:08:00 -0500
Subject: Geo execution and data sovereignty checklist

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Ava Health is keen on Redwood but our security team needs a short checklist about where PII and model inference actually run and whether any data leaves our control. A few concrete questions to start: 

1) For hosted API calls, what geographic regions could host the inference execution and temporary caches (US/Europe/other)?
2) Which subprocessors (cloud providers, logging, analytics, monitoring) might see telemetry or logs tied to request IDs?
3) Do you have a flow for cross-border transfers and subprocessors that shows when data may transit outside the EU?
4) What are retention windows for request inputs, KV caches, and audit logs, and how are deletions handled?

We need a short, plain-language answer for procurement and a slightly deeper technical appendix for our engineers. Can you send both?

Appreciate it — if easier we can jump on a quick call next week.

Best,
Julian Morris
Security Lead, Ava Health

Hi Julian — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR answers up front, then I can loop in Aditya for kernel/runtime specifics and an export of our subprocessor inventory.

- Regions: Hosted API runs in customer-selected regions; for Ava Health we can restrict inference to our US regions (IAD, ORD) or EU regions (DUB, FRA) depending on your account setting. We will confirm the model instance locality per request.
- Subprocessors: Cloud infra (AWS for hosted), monitoring (Datadog), logging (S3/CloudWatch), and analytics (Segment) are common subprocessors — I'll attach an up-to-date inventory.
- Transfers: We provide a processing map that shows where data may transit; for EU-restricted flows we can enable region-locked routing and an EU-only processing path.
- Retention & deletion: Request payloads are retained by default for 30 days for debugging; KV caches are ephemeral and kept in-region, retention depends on policy (default 7 days), and audit logs are retained per contract. We support on-demand deletion via API and contractual deletion windows for private deployments.

Attaching a short one-page summary and will follow up with the technical appendix. Would you like the legal/technical appendices combined or split?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo execution and data sovereignty checklist

Marissa / Evelyn — adding the technical detail Julian asked for. Below is a concise appendix we can send to the prospect; I pulled the current values from infra and the subproc register.

1) Inference execution and caching- Hosted API: requests are routed to a model runtime in the selected region set on the customer tenant. Model execution (forward pass) and KV cache live on GPUs in that region.
  - Regions deployed: us-east-1 (IAD), us-east-2 (CLE), eu-west-1 (DUB), eu-central-1 (FRA), asia-southeast-1 (SIN) — presence depends on account enabled regions.
  - Multi-region fallback: if a specific region lacks capacity, we route per policy to the next compatible region; routing policy can be configured to avoid cross-border fallback.

2) Subprocessors and what they see- Cloud infra: AWS (EC2, EBS) hosts runtime; control plane metadata stored in a separate multi-region control plane (customer metadata encrypted).
  - Logging: Logs are ingested to CloudWatch/S3; access is restricted by IAM. Request IDs are the primary link between logs and requests; we can redact or tokenise request inputs at ingest to prevent full payload persistence.
  - Monitoring & metrics: Datadog receives aggregated telemetry (no full request content).
  - Analytics: Segment is used for opt-in usage analytics; we can disable this per account.

3) Cross-border transfer flows- Default hosted flow: client -> regional frontend -> regional runtime -> optional cross-region fallback -> control plane (metadata) replicated for operational purposes.
  - EU-only option: enable "region lock" and disable cross-border fallback; control plane metadata replication to non-EU regions can be switched off for EU-sensitive accounts (requires Dedicated or Private deployment for strict guarantees).

4) Retention & deletion mechanics- Request inputs: default 30 days; can be lowered to 0 days for sensitive accounts. Deletion API removes records from primary stores and enqueues cache invalidation.
  - KV cache: ephemeral, stored in-memory or SSD local to the GPU node, typically retained 24–168 hours depending on policy; we can offer zero-KV mode (stateless inference) for high-sensitivity customers.
  - Audit logs: retained 90 days by default; contractual SLAs available for longer retention.
  - Deletion verification: we provide deletion receipts and a hashed audit trail indicating deletion timestamps; for Dedicated/Private we can provide proof of deletion on request during audits.

5) Artifacts I attached: subprocessors-inventory.csv (current list and contact points) and a one-page processing map.

If you want, I can also produce a short sequence diagram showing request hops for an EU-only flow and a US->EU fallback flow.

—Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: subprocessors-inventory.csv (text/csv)]

Julian — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise prospect-ready checklist and the processing map Aditya referenced. Highlights:

- We can reduce default retention windows (request inputs to 0 days) and disable analytics for Ava Health during onboarding.
- We offer on-demand deletion API and deletion receipts for audit evidence; for formal audits we can provide the subprocessors inventory and SOC2 summary.
